text:
Sasha: Hey team — presales ask from FinHealth. They need a POC with tenant pinned to eu-west-1 and ca-central-1 for data residency. Questions: can we guarantee routing to those regions only (no cross-border egress), does our subprocessor list cover CA datacenters, and whats the pricing delta + BYOK KMS support?

Marta: Thanks Sasha. Looping in Ingrid (ops) and Leo (runtime). FinHealth is in advanced deal stage, so timing matters — they want answers by EOD Friday.

Ingrid: Quick ops note: we currently support AWS eu-west-1 and GCP ca-central1; subprocessors include AWS, GCP, and our networking partner FastPeering. Legal needs to confirm if FastPeering has CA residency controls. I can pull the subproc attestation doc — ETA 48–72h.

Leo: Tech details: we offer tenant_affinity at region level. For Hosted tier it's "preference" (best-effort) with fallback to nearest eligible region during capacity pressure. For Dedicated we can enforce strict pinning and deny cross-region routing.

Leo: Example config we can propose for the POC:

```json
{
  "tenant_affinity": true,
  "preferred_regions": ["eu-west-1","ca-central1"],
  "fallback_policy": "deny", // deny or failover-to-region
  "kms_mode": "customer_byo_kms"
}
```

Marta: Important for the buyer: Hosted strict-deny isn't guaranteed. We should be explicit in quote. For Dedicated: +30% commit for multi-region reserved capacity. BYOK + one-time integration fee (estimate $5k) and monthly key ops overhead (+$1k/mo).

Sasha: Can we get a short blurb Ingrid for the security questionnaire: which certifications and timeline for subproc attestation?

Ingrid: We have SOC2 Type II, ISO27001, and GDPR DPIA completed. Subproc attestation for FastPeering/CA region I'll escalate — expect a signed attestation PDF in 2–3 business days.

Sasha: Leo — can you confirm the network path (no egress to US) if we set fallback_policy: "deny" on Dedicated? Also how about replica KV caches (are they kept region-local)?

Leo: On Dedicated with strict pinning, traffic stays in-region and KV caches are per-region; no cross-region replication unless customer opts in. On Hosted with deny fallback we'll return 429/503 when capacity unavailable (configurable).

Marta: I'll prepare two options to share with the customer:
- Option A (Hosted, geo-preference): lower ops, best-effort, fallback to nearest; no hard guarantee.
- Option B (Dedicated, strict pin): enforce residency, + pricing, BYOK supported, SLA.

Sasha: Perfect. Also legal asked about subprocessors list versioning — Ingrid, can you attach the current list and the date?

Ingrid: Attached will be subproc_list_2026-03-23.pdf. I'll drop it in the deal doc and link it here once uploaded.

DeployBot: Created presales ticket PRESALES-4821 for FinHealth POC (assignee: Marta).

Marta: I'll draft the quote and include the BYOK integration line items. Sasha — can you flag the PO so finance can fast-track? :pray:

Sasha: Done, flagged with finance. Quick note: buyer also asked for an answer on data deletion flow on contract termination — include retention and crypto-key destruction steps in the response.

Ingrid: We'll include retention policy + KMS key rotation/destruction steps.

Leo: I'll add a short tech appendix about routing behavior and KV locality to the POC runbook.

Marta: Targeting customer update by Friday EOD. If anything stalls earlier, ping me. :thumbsup:
